read.title: Should Homework Be Banned?
read.text: The debate over homework is increasingly controversial. Some educators claim that hours of assignments after school deny children time to play, rest and develop independent interests. Others insist that homework builds discipline and reinforces what was taught in class. A comprehensive review of studies found that moderate homework benefits high-school students, while its value for young children is hardly measurable.

q.q: What did the comprehensive review find?
o: Homework has no value at any age.

q.q: What do supporters of homework claim?

read.title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
read.text: Artificial intelligence can now compose music, diagnose diseases and predict consumer behavior. Yet its rapid development raises difficult dilemmas. Who is responsible when an algorithm makes a deadly mistake? Can a system trained on biased data avoid discrimination? Experts urge governments to impose clear guidelines before the technology becomes impossible to control.

q.q: What do experts urge governments to do?
Which concern is raised in the text?
q.a: Algorithms trained on biased data may discriminate.

read.title: Saving the Dead Sea
read.text: The Dead Sea is shrinking by more than a meter every year. Because water from the Jordan River is diverted for agriculture and drinking, far less reaches the sea. Massive sinkholes have appeared along the shore, swallowing roads and buildings. Proposed solutions include a canal from the Red Sea, but environmentalists fear the consequences of mixing two very different bodies of water.

q.q: Why is the Dead Sea shrinking?
q.a: Less water from the Jordan River reaches it.

q.q: Why do environmentalists object to the canal?
q.a: They fear the effects of mixing different waters.

read.title: The Power of Habits
read.text: Psychologists estimate that nearly half of our daily actions are habits rather than conscious decisions. Every habit follows a cycle: a cue, a routine and a reward. To change a bad habit, it is not enough to rely on determination. Instead, experts suggest keeping the cue and the reward but replacing the routine—for example, going for a walk instead of reaching for a snack when stressed.

q.q: What is the cycle of a habit?
How can we change a bad habit, according to experts?
q.a: Replace the routine but keep the cue and reward.

read.title: Languages in Danger
read.text: Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken today, linguists predict that nearly half could disappear by the end of the century. When the last speaker of a language dies, a unique way of seeing the world is lost. Some communities are fighting back: they record elderly speakers, publish dictionaries and teach the language in schools. The revival of Hebrew is often cited as an exceptional success.

q.q: What happens when a language disappears?
q.a: A unique way of seeing the world is lost.
o: A new language replaces it immediately.

q.q: Which language is cited as a success story?

read.title: The Gig Economy
read.text: Millions of people now earn a living through apps, delivering food or driving passengers. Supporters praise the flexibility: workers can choose their own hours. Critics, however, point out that these workers often lack basic protections such as sick pay or pensions. Several countries are debating legislation that would entitle app workers to the same rights as regular employees.

q.q: What do supporters of the gig economy praise?
What would the proposed legislation do?
q.a: Give app workers the same rights as employees.

read.title: Space Tourism
read.text: A ticket to the edge of space currently costs hundreds of thousands of dollars, yet waiting lists are long. Supporters argue that space tourism will boost exploration and make spaceflight cheaper for everyone. Opponents question whether such expensive trips are justified while urgent problems remain on Earth, and they warn about the environmental impact of frequent rocket launches.

o: It is good for the climate.

q.a: The environmental impact of rocket launches.

read.title: The Invisible Gorilla
read.text: In a famous experiment, participants watched a video of people passing a basketball and were asked to count the passes. Halfway through, a person in a gorilla costume walked across the scene. Astonishingly, about half of the viewers failed to notice it. The study illustrates how focusing intensely on one task can make us blind to the obvious.

q.q: What were participants asked to do?

q.a: Intense focus can make us miss obvious things.
